Woke Evangelicalism
WOHK ee-van-JEL-uh-kal-iz-um
noun (contemporary theological-cultural phenomenon)
Mid-2010s through early 2020s evangelical-adjacent phenomenon adopting progressive social-justice categories (race, gender, intersectionality, structural injustice) into evangelical theology and church practice. Term woke derives from African-American Vernacular English (stay woke); applied to broader progressive social-justice consciousness; used pejoratively by critical-theory critics. Principal expressions: George Floyd-era racial-reconciliation discourse, Critical Race Theory in evangelical seminaries, the broader Christianity-Today / Russell Moore / David French wing.

📖 Biblical Definition

Mid-2010s through early 2020s evangelical-adjacent phenomenon adopting progressive social-justice categories (race, gender, intersectionality, structural injustice) into evangelical theology and church practice. The term woke derives from African-American Vernacular English (stay woke, originally meaning alert to systemic injustice); was applied to broader progressive social-justice consciousness in the 2010s; and is used pejoratively by critical-theory critics. Principal expressions of woke evangelicalism include (1) racial-reconciliation discourse in the wake of the George Floyd protests (2020) and the broader Black Lives Matter moment, including the MLK50 conference (2018), Together for the Gospel's various statements, and the Southern Baptist Convention's 2019 Resolution 9 on Critical Race Theory; (2) Critical Race Theory and broader critical-theory categories adopted into evangelical seminaries and institutions (Southern Seminary's controversial period, Southeastern Seminary, the broader academic-evangelical scene); (3) the broader Christianity Today editorial trajectory under Mark Galli (2013-2019, culminating in the 2019 anti-Trump editorial) and continuing under subsequent editors; (4) Russell Moore's tenure as president of the Southern Baptist Convention's Ethics and Religious Liberty Commission (2013-2021) and his subsequent move to Christianity Today; (5) the David French / Ekstasis-orbit anti-Trump never-Trump evangelical political tradition. The Reformed-confessional and broader patriarchal-Reformed response has been sharp critique. The Statement on Social Justice and the Gospel (the so-called Dallas Statement, 2018, signed by John MacArthur and many others) and the broader Just Thinking podcast (Darrell Harrison and Virgil Walker) and Voddie Baucham (Fault Lines, 2021) have been principal voices critiquing the woke-evangelical trajectory as a substantive departure from biblical anthropology, soteriology, and ethics. The patriarchal-Reformed reader receives woke evangelicalism as a serious contemporary distortion of evangelical theology and stands with the substantive Reformed-confessional critique.

WOKE EVANGELICALISM, n. (contemporary theological-cultural phenomenon; mid-2010s-early-2020s) Evangelical-adjacent phenomenon adopting progressive social-justice categories (race, gender, intersectionality, structural injustice) into evangelical theology and church practice. Principal expressions: racial-reconciliation discourse post-George Floyd (2020); CRT in evangelical seminaries; SBC Resolution 9 (2019); Christianity Today editorial trajectory under Galli (2013-2019, anti-Trump editorial); Russell Moore at ERLC (2013-2021) and subsequent CT move; David French / Ekstasis never-Trump evangelical tradition. Critique: Statement on Social Justice and the Gospel (Dallas Statement, 2018, MacArthur and others); Voddie Baucham's Fault Lines (2021); Just Thinking podcast (Harrison and Walker).

📖 Key Scripture

Galatians 3:28 — "There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus."

Ephesians 2:14-16 — "For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us; Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; for to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace; And that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross, having slain the enmity thereby."

2 Corinthians 5:17 — "Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new."

1 Corinthians 1:10 — "Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Woke evangelicalism imports progressive social-justice categories (CRT, intersectionality, structural injustice) into evangelical theology; departs from biblical anthropology, soteriology, ethics; critiqued by Dallas Statement (2018) and Baucham's Fault Lines (2021).

expand to see more

Woke evangelicalism's substantive doctrinal corruption is the importation of progressive social-justice categories (Critical Race Theory, intersectionality, structural injustice analysis, oppressor-oppressed binary readings of social relations) into evangelical theology and church practice. The result is a series of substantive departures from historic Christian doctrine. (1) Anthropological: humans are increasingly categorized first by race, gender, and intersectional identity rather than by their fundamental identity as image-bearers of God under His covenant. (2) Soteriological: the gospel is increasingly reframed as deliverance from social-structural oppression rather than as deliverance from sin, wrath, and judgment through Christ's substitutionary atonement. (3) Ethical: biblical sexual ethics, biblical sex-distinctions, and biblical authority structures are progressively softened or abandoned under the pressure of progressive social-justice critique.

The Reformed-confessional and broader patriarchal-Reformed critique has been sharp and substantive. The Statement on Social Justice and the Gospel (the Dallas Statement, 2018, drafted by John MacArthur, Phil Johnson, James White, Voddie Baucham, and others) provides the formal theological articulation. Voddie Baucham's Fault Lines: The Social Justice Movement and Evangelicalism's Looming Catastrophe (2021) provides the substantive book-length critique with extensive analysis of Critical Race Theory's incompatibility with biblical anthropology and soteriology. The patriarchal-Reformed reader receives woke evangelicalism as a serious contemporary distortion and stands with the substantive Reformed-confessional critique. The answer is the historic-confessional gospel of God's free grace in Christ to undeserving sinners of every race, sex, and station — not the progressive social-justice gospel of structural-oppression deliverance through critical-theory consciousness.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Mid-2010s-early-2020s; CRT and intersectionality in evangelical theology; Dallas Statement 2018; Baucham's Fault Lines 2021.
